title: A repeated ASR token from a real speech disfluency shifts token indices
why_real: Speakers repeat a word when they stumble ('ask ask diksha'), and the ASR faithfully transcribes both repetitions while the formatter only keeps one, so the token counts diverge exactly like they do for filler words.

inputs.asr: ask ask diksha for the file

expected.reason: Sequence alignment resolves the repeated ASR token to a single formatted token and still finds the right memory.
